verdict: DaVita grew revenue 5% to $3.6B and lifted profit attributable to its shareholders 48% to $223M — even after booking a $62M impairment charge on its China business.

segments.name: Dialysis patient services
segments.note: Payments for dialysis treatments — filtering blood for people whose kidneys no longer can — mostly from Medicare and insurers. Up 3% on annual rate increases and a better payor mix; DaVita ran 7.33M U.S. treatments at $415 of revenue each.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Everything else — mainly international dialysis and related care services. Up 39% as the overseas business grows.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — management, IT, billing and support. Roughly flat YoY.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of dialysis centers and equipment over their lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Impairment & other, net
opex.note: A $62M non-cash impairment charge on the China business, partly offset by $8M of income from equity investments.

otherDetail: Other expense of $187M, net: $150M of debt expense (interest on borrowings), less $9M of other income — and it also includes the $46M share of profit belonging to noncontrolling partners in DaVita's joint-venture clinics, so the flow lands on the $223M attributable to DaVita shareholders.
footerNote: Adaptation: patient care costs are the direct cost of revenue; the rest mirrors DaVita's income statement (the $62M impairment is shown net of $8M of equity investment income). Net income is the $223M attributable to DaVita Inc. (total net income was $269M, of which $46M belongs to noncontrolling interests), matching the $3.40 diluted EPS. Figures are rounded to $M from thousands in the release.
oneTimers: A $62M non-cash goodwill and asset impairment charge on DaVita's China business sits inside operating costs. Excluding it, adjusted operating income was $561M (vs $499M reported) and adjusted EPS was $3.82 (vs $3.40).

takeaways.title: EPS jumped two-thirds
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose from $2.04 to $3.40. Buybacks helped — DaVita repurchased 0.6M shares for $111M in the quarter, and the diluted share count is down from 73.8M to 65.5M in a year — and a smaller share of profit went to joint-venture partners.

takeaways.title: China write-down hit operating profit
takeaways.text: Operating income was $499M, slightly below last year's $506M, because of a $62M non-cash impairment on the China business. Without it, adjusted operating income was $561M, a 15.7% margin.

takeaways.title: Steady treatments, better rates
takeaways.text: Revenue per U.S. treatment was $415.25, up from $405.15 a year ago, while treatment volume grew just 0.4% on a normalized basis. Revenue growth is coming from price and mix, not from many more patients.
